beats.title: Identify the right postulate
beats.instruction: Study the figure. Segment BD is shared by △ABD and △CBD. AB ≅ CB (given tick marks) and AD ≅ CD (given tick marks). Drag the label to the correct postulate box to identify which postulate proves △ABD ≅ △CBD.
beats.successMessage: Correct! AB ≅ CB, BD ≅ BD (Reflexive), AD ≅ CD — that is SSS. △ABD ≅ △CBD by SSS.

steps.text: Statement: AB ≅ CB. Reason: Given. (The tick marks in the figure show this is provided as given information.)
Statement: AD ≅ CD. Reason: Given. (Second pair of given congruent sides.)
Statement: BD ≅ BD. Reason: Reflexive Property of Congruence. (Any segment is congruent to itself.)
Statement: △ABD ≅ △CBD. Reason: SSS Congruence Postulate. (All three pairs of sides are congruent.)
Statement: ∠ABD ≅ ∠CBD. Reason: CPCTC. (Corresponding angles of congruent triangles are congruent — BD bisects ∠ABC.)

items.prompt: In a two-column proof, the left column contains _______ and the right column contains _______.
items.explanation: Two-column proofs: left = Statements (what is true), right = Reasons (why it is true — given info, definitions, postulates, theorems).

items.prompt: In a triangle congruence proof, which reason allows you to say a segment is congruent to itself?
items.explanation: The Reflexive Property states that any figure is congruent to itself: AB ≅ AB. This is used when two triangles share a common side.

items.prompt: Given: AB ∥ CD, BC ∥ AD (parallelogram ABCD). Diagonal AC is drawn. The plan is to prove △ABC ≅ △CDA. What is the most efficient postulate, using the alternate interior angles created by the parallel lines?
hints: AB ∥ CD means alternate interior angles ∠BAC and ∠DCA are congruent (cut by transversal AC).
BC ∥ AD means ∠BCA and ∠DAC are congruent (cut by transversal AC). AC is shared.
Two angle pairs (∠BAC ≅ ∠DCA, ∠BCA ≅ ∠DAC) and included side AC → ASA.

items.prompt: In a proof, after △PQR ≅ △STU is established by SAS, a student needs to show QR ≅ TU. The correct reason is…
hints: QR and TU were not part of the given information or the SAS setup.
They are corresponding sides in the proven-congruent triangles.
After proving triangle congruence, use CPCTC to claim corresponding parts are congruent.

items.prompt: A proof has these statements and reasons so far: (1) ∠A ≅ ∠D — Given; (2) ∠B ≅ ∠E — Given; (3) AB ≅ DE — Given. The next statement should be…
hints: Three pieces of given info: two angles and a side. Where is the side?
AB is between ∠A and ∠B — it is the included side.
Two angles (∠A, ∠B) and included side AB → ASA. So △ABC ≅ △DEF by ASA.

items.prompt: Which property justifies the step 'since M is the midpoint of XZ, XM ≅ MZ'?
hints: A midpoint divides a segment into two congruent halves.
By definition, a midpoint creates two equal segments: XM ≅ MZ.

annotations.text: AB ≅ CB (given), AD ≅ CD (given), BD ≅ BD (Reflexive)
Two-Column Proof: △ABD ≅ △CBD by SSS → ∠ABD ≅ ∠CBD by CPCTC

testItems.prompt: In a two-column proof, what appears in the 'Reasons' column?
choices: Definitions, postulates, theorems, and given information that justify each statement

testItems.prompt: A proof gives: (1) PQ ≅ RS — Given; (2) QR ≅ QR — Reflexive Property; (3) PR ≅ SQ — Given. The next step proves △PQR ≅ △SRQ. What is the reason?
To prove that the diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other, you use the triangles formed by the diagonals. What is the role of CPCTC in this proof?
choices: To conclude the half-diagonal segments are congruent, after the triangles are proven congruent
To establish the right angles at the intersection

testItems.prompt: Which sequence of reasons is in the correct logical order for a triangle congruence proof that ends with a CPCTC conclusion?
Given isosceles △ABC with AB ≅ AC, and M the midpoint of BC. A proof draws AM. What is the most efficient path to prove ∠ABM ≅ ∠ACM?
choices: Prove △ABM ≅ △ACM by SSS, then use CPCTC
Use the Isosceles Triangle Theorem directly without triangles
Prove △ABM ≅ △ACM by AAS, then use CPCTC
Apply SAS directly to the angles

testItems.prompt: In a proof, a student has: AB ≅ CD (given), ∠ABE ≅ ∠CDE (given), ∠AEB ≅ ∠CED (vertical angles). The student writes '△ABE ≅ △CDE by ASA.' Is this correct?
choices: Yes — ∠ABE, AB, and ∠AEB with correspondence A↔C, B↔D, E↔E
No — the two angles ∠ABE and ∠AEB are at the endpoints of AB, making AB the included side. This is ASA. But ∠CDE and ∠CED are at the endpoints of CD. The correspondence holds.
No — vertical angles cannot be used in proofs
Yes — and the reason is AAS, not ASA

testItems.prompt: Proof goal: 'In △ABC, if BD is the angle bisector of ∠ABC and is also the perpendicular bisector of AC, prove that △ABC is isosceles.' Which congruence tools are needed?
choices: SAS to prove △ABD ≅ △CBD, then CPCTC to conclude AB ≅ CB
HL to prove △ABD ≅ △CBD, then CPCTC to conclude AB ≅ CB
SSS to prove △ABD ≅ △CBD, then CPCTC to conclude AB ≅ CB
AAS to prove △ABD ≅ △CBD, then CPCTC to conclude AB ≅ CB
testItems.explanation: BD ⊥ AC (perpendicular bisector) gives right angles at D; AD ≅ DC (midpoint); BD ≅ BD (Reflexive). But right triangles + hypotenuse AB=CB (goal) + leg AD=CD → HL proves them congruent; then AB ≅ CB by CPCTC.
